o1.biggest_strength: It finds the main lever in the data, makes the pause the critical path, stops wasting discounts on trip-over customers, and gives product a buildable one-screen flow with usable copy.
o1.biggest_mistake: The forecast slightly overreaches on the untested reminder/plan-switch assumptions and appears to count all not-progress cancellers in the reminder estimate, not just the 72% without reminders.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the maths by reason, separate proven from assumed uplift, and make the revenue table fully auditable line by line.

o2.biggest_strength: It is clear, practical, and gets the big ideas right: bring back pause, use the annual plan for price objections, and use reminders for progress problems.
o2.biggest_mistake: It keeps the 50% discount for switchers without evidence, which is exactly the sort of margin leak this new flow should avoid; it also muddles the required reason with an 'always live' cancel button.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Remove the unsupported discount, make every reason panel visibly include the cancel button, and clean up the assumptions so the forecast is less optimistic and easier to trust.

reason: Output 1 is the one I would hand to product first: it puts the proven pause first, avoids lazy discounts, and calls out the critical path and risk. Output 2 is usable, but I would challenge the discount for switchers and the cancel-button logic before building it.
